summary: Teardown of a two-list buffer structure. The second list (head at this+0x10) is walked and freed, freeing each node's owned data block first when the node's +8 flag and +0 data pointer are both non-zero. The first list (head at this+0x0) is then walked; flagged nodes whose data block starts with a non-null callback-block pointer run NTimeCallbackLoopWithSEH over 4156-byte entries with the block's own entry count and EmptyStub_aa60, then free the block header and data block. All eight list bookkeeping fields are cleared after teardown.

operations.description: Iterate the second linked list whose head is this[4] (byte offset +0x10), following each node's next pointer at node+4 until the chain is exhausted.
For each second-list node, test the flag byte at node+8 and the data pointer at node+0; both non-zero means the node owns a heap data block that must be freed first.
Free the second-list node's owned data block through FreeWrapper_7bcf.
Free each second-list node itself through FreeWrapper_7bcf.
Clear the second-list bookkeeping fields this+0x10, +0x14, +0x18 and +0x1C to 0.
Iterate the first linked list whose head is this[0] (byte offset +0x0), following each node's next pointer at node+4 until the chain is exhausted.
For each first-list node, test the flag byte at node+8; only flagged nodes get data cleanup before the node is freed.
When the flagged node's data pointer at node+0 is non-null and its first DWORD is non-null, treat that first DWORD as a callback-block pointer.

Run NTimeCallbackLoopWithSEH over the callback block with 4156-byte entries, the block's own entry count (the DWORD immediately before the block) and EmptyStub_aa60 as the callback; afterwards free the block header and the data block through FreeWrapper_7bcf.
Free each first-list node itself through FreeWrapper_7bcf.
Clear the first-list bookkeeping fields this+0x0, +0x4, +0x8 and +0xC to 0.
Return after both linked lists are freed and all list bookkeeping fields are cleared.
